cards.explanation: The plan is that Ahab goes disguised and Jehoshaphat wears his royal robes. Ahab, king of Israel, says, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes." Jehoshaphat is king of Judah, so he's the one dressed like a king. I think his closet was about to get way more attention than he ever wanted, friends.

The answer is Israel. The king of Aram orders his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel." That's a short list of one, friends. Every commander knows exactly who he's looking for.

The answer is True. The chariot commanders see Jehoshaphat and say, "Surely this is the king of Israel!" Then they turn to fight against him. They're doing what their king ordered, and they think they found their man.

The answer is that he cries out, and that's all the text tells us he does. The chariot commanders are turning on him, and Jehoshaphat just hollers. I bet that was one loud, very sincere holler, friends. Then the commanders see that he is not the king of Israel and turn back.

The answer is False. When the chariot commanders saw that Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel, they "…turned back from pursuing him." Their order was about the king of Israel, and this wasn't him. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, got to breathe again, friends.

The answer is the king of Israel. A certain man draws his bow "…without taking special aim…" and the arrow strikes Ahab between the joints of his armor. Ahab went in disguised, and an arrow with no special aim still found him. This is a heavy turn in the story, friends, so let's take it in quietly.

The answer is True. Ahab says to his charioteer, "Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am badly wounded!" That's the king of Israel speaking, in his own words. I think this one hurts a little to read, friends.

The answer is evening. The text says Ahab was propped up in his chariot, facing the Arameans, and "…that evening he died." It's a long day for everybody out there. This is a heavy moment, friends, so we'll just say it plainly.

The answer is True. As the sun was setting, a cry rang out in the army: "Every man to his own city, and every man to his own land!" The call is for the men to go back to their own cities and lands. It's a fitting end to a very long day, friends.

The answer is the word the LORD had spoken. The text says the dogs licked up Ahab's blood "…according to the word that the LORD had spoken." So what happened at the pool of Samaria matches what the LORD said. When the LORD speaks, it stands, friends.

The answer is his son Ahaziah. The text says Ahab rested with his fathers, "…and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place." So the crown stays in the family. And this is the last verse of the passage, friends, so Ahab's story wraps up here.
